competitors.name: Ramco Aviation (MRO/ERP software, warranty management module)
competitors.what_they_do: Full aircraft maintenance and materials ERP that lists 'Warranty Management' as a feature. Its FAQ claims customers 'achieve up to $6 million in savings on warranty claims'. The page names no customer, gives no detail on how vendor-repair warranty claims work, and I saw no contingency or done-for-you claim filing. This is the only competitor I could verify. It is software you run yourself, sold to large operators, not an outsourced success-fee auditor.
competitors.scale_or_funding: Established enterprise vendor (part of Ramco Systems, listed in India). The claim is marketing copy and I could not verify it.

white_space: Caveat: this verdict rests on thin evidence. The WebSearch budget was exhausted (200 of 200) after the first two lookups. Every further search was refused, and I did not work around that limit. I could only fetch vendor homepages directly. I found no dedicated contingency-fee warranty auditor for rotable repair claims. I also could not rule one out, because I could not run Crunchbase, YC, Product Hunt or 'startup + key terms' searches. Vendor pages I checked (Trax eMRO, Veryon/Rusada, Pentagon 2000, CAMP) showed no warranty-claims features on their homepages, but homepage silence is weak evidence. I could not check IFS Maintenix (HTTP 429). Gaps that look unserved: (1) an outsourced, success-fee service that reads unstructured repair-invoice PDFs and joins them to removal records. This is the cross-system join the idea describes. (2) Small and mid-size operators such as regionals, Part 135 fleets and air-ambulance operators, which sit below the large ERP buyers Ramco targets. (3) The adjacent leaks, meaning no-fault-found fees within warranty, unreturned core penalties and turnaround-time guarantee credits. None of the vendor pages I read mention these. Unverified risks from my own domain knowledge, not from research: power-by-the-hour and maintenance-service-plan contracts remove warranty exposure for many small fleets. Shop warranty terms are often short and carry exclusions. Getting AP and maintenance-system exports from a small operator is hard. The addressable market may be small. Someone should check all of these before building.
evidence_of_demand: Essentially none found. I could not run forum, RFP or regulation searches because the search budget was exhausted. The only indirect signal is Ramco's marketing claim of 'up to $6 million in savings on warranty claims' (https://www.ramco.com/aviation). It suggests warranty recovery is treated as a valued outcome. It is unattributed, so it is not proof that anyone pays for outsourced recovery. I found no evidence yet of operators paying contingency fees for this, of RFPs, or of forum complaints about unclaimed rotable warranties.
kill_reason: n/a. Nothing found so far justifies a kill, but the research was incomplete. Re-run the existence check with a restored search budget before committing. Priority searches: 'aircraft component warranty recovery services', 'airline warranty audit contingency', Crunchbase/YC/Product Hunt for aviation warranty startups, and operator complaints about unclaimed repair warranties.
sharper_angle: Start with a wedge that needs only the accounts-payable export, so you avoid the hardest data-access problem, which is integrating with each operator's maintenance system. Run a 'repeat-repair detector' on repair invoices. Flag any part number and serial number that comes back to the same shop within the warranty window, and flag no-fault-found evaluation fees, core-return penalties and late-turnaround credits on the same invoices. This works the way freight and telecom audit firms do: an AP file in, a claims list out, paid only on credits recovered. Sell it first to Part 145 shops and parts pools that buy many exchange units, and to lessors and asset managers who need warranty compliance across a portfolio. Regionals and EMS operators can come later. Add the maintenance-system removal data as a second phase to confirm failures the invoices alone cannot show. Position it as outsourced claim filing and vendor negotiation, which ERP warranty modules like Ramco's do not provide, and not as software.
